cards.summary: Copies the selection to the clipboard.
Select an object, press S, then drag to resize it. Click once before dragging to choose a different origin.
cards.but: Unlike Figma Scale, Illustrator scales strokes and effects only when Scale Strokes & Effects is enabled in its scaling settings.

cards.summary: Draws a rectangle. Hold Shift for a square.
Draws an ellipse. Hold Shift for a circle.

cards.but: L in Illustrator is the Ellipse tool, not Line.

cards.summary: An artboard sets the area of a design, like a top-level frame.
cards.but: This is an approximate match for a design area. An Illustrator artboard does not provide Figma Frame's container and auto layout behavior.
To show them again, use Cmd+Option+3. It shows everything you hid.

cards.summary: Locks the selected objects so they can't be clicked.
cards.but: To unlock, use Cmd+Option+2. It unlocks everything at once.

cards.summary: Copy, then Paste in Front puts the copy exactly on top.
cards.but: Cmd+D in Illustrator is Transform Again: it repeats the last transformation. Use Copy, then Paste in Front to duplicate; this updates your clipboard.

cards.summary: Toggles the rulers along the canvas edges.
Fits the current artboard in the window.
cards.but: Cmd+0 fits the active artboard only. Cmd+Option+0 fits all of them.
To select points inside a path, use the Direct Selection tool (A).

cards.summary: Adds text. Click for point text, drag for a text box.
Figma auto layout responds to content changes. Illustrator's Align and Distribute commands are manual alternatives.
cards.noMatchAlternative: Line things up with the Align panel (Window → Align).
